result.title: What Is the Influence of Task Order in Continual Learning? An Empirical Study and Order-Aware Evaluation for Motion Forecasting
result.summary: Aggregate scores for continual learning algorithms rest on a distribution over task orders that is rarely stated. We formulate algorithm comparison as an expectation over a declared order distribution, which separates training variation from order variation, and apply it to motion forecasting with four road-layout tasks from the INTERACTION dataset, all 24 task orders, four algorithms, and three training replicates (288 runs). Task order accounts for 65\% to 91\% of the variation in current-task error and backward transfer, and 90\% to 99\% of this order effect comes from the identity of the starting task: the smallest task cannot be learned from a cold start. Beyond the first stage, the order effect is comparable to training variability. In most orders, the leading algorithm in current-task error and backward transfer is within one replicate standard deviation of the runner-up. Backward transfer depends on the order mainly through its reference term, which weights the first task most heavily, so relative improvement and final error identify different leading algorithms for displacement error. A transition-direction descriptor computed from task statistics tracks the position of the smallest task, and weighting orders by it leaves the algorithm ranking unchanged. These results call for benchmarks that declare their order distribution and report order-resolved, starting-task-resolved, warm-start, and final errors alongside aggregate scores. The code and data are available \href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/task-order-cl-4f7b/}{here}.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在运动预测任务上系统量化持续学习中的任务顺序效应：用 INTERACTION 数据集的四种道路布局任务、全部 24 种顺序、四种算法和三次重复共 288 次运行，将算法比较表述为对已声明顺序分布的期望，并报告顺序分辨与起始任务分辨的评价。
AI.relevance_reason: 顺序可解释当前任务误差与后向迁移的 65%–91%，且多来自起始任务；这一「把顺序变异与训练变异分离、并显式声明评价分布」的思路，可能为多阶段训练 VLM 推理能力时的顺序效应与贡献/评价归因提供核查线索。
